messages:
Alex (Sales): hey team, Spruce reported intermittent spikes in first-token latency during their POC this morning. They see ~20–40ms normally but occasional 600–900ms on first token after idle. cc @Kevin (Spruce)
Maria (Eng): thanks. is this happening on hosted or their dedicated test pool? any recent config changes? can you paste a request id or logs? :thinking_face:
Kevin (Spruce): hosted via our trial account (region: us-west-2). No config changes on our side. Here's the response headers from one slow request: 
  x-request-id: rq_02f4ab3c
  x-rl-remaining: 49
  x-model: small-llama-v1
  x-serving-mode: shared
Headers were same for fast requests.
Jamie (Support): can you also paste the full server log around rq_02f4ab3c? even a short excerpt with timestamps helps.
Kevin (Spruce): pasted log snippet: 
```
2026-03-20T14:01:12.123Z INFO request rq_02f4ab3c recv
2026-03-20T14:01:12.128Z DEBUG model small-llama-v1 kv_cache_lookup miss key=conv-72
2026-03-20T14:01:12.210Z INFO batching queued batch_id=821 size=8 wait_ms=82
2026-03-20T14:01:12.412Z INFO dispatch start batch_id=821
2026-03-20T14:01:12.986Z INFO token 1 emitted latency_ms=863
```
Maria (Eng): that log is telling — kv_cache_lookup miss then batching queued wait of 82ms and dispatch latency leads to big ttft. Two things likely happening: (1) cold KV cache on shared serving node, (2) batching wait for throughput spikes. Both increase TTFT. The 863ms token emission is dominated by queue + model startup.
Maria (Eng): quick repro question: does the spike happen only after a long idle (~>30m)? Kevin?
Kevin (Spruce): yes usually after ~45–90m idle. During steady traffic it's fine.
Maria (Eng): that aligns with prefix/KV eviction after idle. Workarounds we recommend: 
- enable lightweight warmup (prefill) for POC using a small synthetic prefill on session start, e.g. prefill 128 tokens to populate KV cache.
- reduce batching latency by setting batch_time_ms to 1–5ms for low-latency routes or set max_batch_size to 1 for strict TTFT.
- pin traffic to Dedicated for predictable warm nodes if they need consistent low TTFT at scale.
Jamie (Support): for hosted customers we can push a per-route override: 
```
route_override: {"max_batch_size":1, "batch_time_ms":5, "prefill_tokens":128}
```
Would you like us to enable that for Spruce trial? (we can roll back anytime)
Kevin (Spruce): yes please try route override for their low-latency endpoint. Also curious about cost impact — prefill tokens will bill, right?
Alex (Sales): short answer: prefill tokens count as normal tokens (billed), but for a POC the extra cost is usually small; we can offer trial credits if they want to experiment.
Sasha (Security): quick security Q: if we enable prefill, where do the prefill prompts come from? Are we sending any customer data to third-party services? We need to confirm no telemetry leak.
Maria (Eng): prefill is executed within the same serving runtime and uses the customer's prompt template. No external services involved. For hosted we keep prefill data in-memory for warm caches and do not persist model inputs to external storage. We can also use ephemeral prefill text (synthetic filler) if they prefer no real user data.
DevBot: deploy-event: route-override/spruce-lowlatency started by jamie.support at 2026-03-20T14:12:00Z :rocket:
Jamie (Support): override applied to the sprue-llm-route. Please test and paste a new slow request id if it still happens.
Kevin (Spruce): testing now... new request id rq_02f4b999. Got first token in 58ms. Looks much better. Will stress test over the day and report back.
Maria (Eng): great. FYI if they later want to reduce token billing we can recommend a warmup-only approach (prefill with synthetic tokens that are shorter) or move to Dedicated where we can keep hot nodes and avoid repeated prefill.
Sasha (Security): noted on data handling. I'll draft a short note for their security questionnaire: hosted prefill runs in-customer memory, no external storage, TLS end-to-end, KMS for keys. Will share.
Alex (Sales): action items: (1) jamie: keep override live for 24–48h and watch cost/latency. (2) maria: share docs snippet for route_override and quick commands we used. (3) sasha: add the prefill note for the security questionnaire. (4) kevin: let us know if you see any further spikes. Thanks all :pray:
Kevin (Spruce): thanks team — big improvement. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
